title: Playwright SDK e2e smoke checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook for shipping and running Playwright-based e2e smoke tests against our SDK sampleapps and quickstart flows. Goal is to catch integration regressions that would block a first-time developer (auth, sample app wiring, basic request/response, streaming fallback).

Audience:
- SDK maintainers
- Developer experience engineers
- QA engineers doing release gate checks

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: one-page quickstart checks that can be run locally or in CI to validate basic SDK surface area across node/python sampleapps and the hosted API (auth + simple prompt + embedding).
- Non-goal: exhaustive product e2e, load or perf testing (those belong to separate infra/perf suites).

Why Playwright?
- Cross-language sample apps (JS) are already used in onboarding labs, so Playwright gives reliable browser automation for the quickstart web flows plus API mock harnessing for CLI flows.
- Fast feedback loops: tests are small <10s each in most cases when using recorded network fixtures + prefix caching.

Quickstart (local dev) 
Prereqs: node 18+, npx, docker optional for headless chromium parity, an active dev token (redwood-dev-*) or local proxy running.
Commands:
1) clone sample repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git && cd sdk-samples/playground
2) install: npm ci
3) run sample dev server: REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood-dev-xxx npm run dev (or start local-proxy)
4) run smoke suite: npx playwright test smoke --config=playwright.smoke.config.ts
Notes: smoke config pins to minimal browser (chromium headless), network timeouts shortened, and fixtures enabled so runs are stable offline.

Core smoke scenarios (priority order):
1) First-run onboarding flow (happy path): open /quickstart -> click "Run in browser" -> enter token -> send a single prompt -> receive streaming response -> UI shows tokens and completion.
2) CLI quickstart wiring: run `node cli-sample.js --prompt \"hello\"` and assert exit code 0 + JSON response shape contains {id, model, tokens}.
3) Embeddings smoke: call embeddings endpoint with small text, assert vector length matches expected dim and not all-zero.
4) Token-limit fallback: simulate long input to ensure SDK switches to chunked-stream path (assert fallback header or telemetry event).
5) Error handling: server returns 401 -> ensure UI shows re-auth prompt and SDK does not crash.
6) Offline cached replay: verify that when prefix caching is enabled, repeated identical prompt returns from cache (fast path metric).

Minimal assertions to include:
- Response shape sanity (id, model, content)
- Latency is under gate? (only in CI smoke: <5s median for sample prompt)
- Telemetry event emitted for `session.start` and `session.complete` with sampling tag, not PII
- Proper error surfaced to UI/CLI (exposed status-code, message)

Telemetry & observability checks (quick):
- Check that smoke tests validate presence of a mock telemetry payload POST to /telemetry with required minimal fields: {event, sdk_version, sample_app, env}. In CI we stub the outbound so we assert payload shape only.
- Tagging: tests should assert presence of `quickstart_smoke=true` in telemetry to differentiate from production.

CI integration suggestions:
- Add a `smoke` job to main pipeline after unit tests but before release tagging. Runs with HEAD token scoped to ephemeral smoke role.
- Use matrix to run node and python sample apps (two rows). Keep runtime under 5 minutes total for cost.
- Flaky handling: if smoke fails, post a summarized report to #devexp-smoke channel and open a short-lived review with automerge blocked.

Failure modes and debug heuristics (notes to self):
- 401s: usually token misconfig or env mismatch. Check infra proxy logs and `REDWOOD_ENV` used by sample app.
- Streaming hangs: check network stub TTL and Playwright waitForResponse timeouts. Add stack traces capture (save HAR + playwright trace) on failure.
- Intermittent embed dims mismatch: likely model variant delta in model catalog. Add explicit model pin in fixtures.

Checklist for adding a new smoke case:
- [ ] small, deterministic input (no randomness)
- [ ] uses fixture or stubbed network where external variability exists
- [ ] contains exactly 1 assertion for success and 1 assertion for telemetry
- [ ] run-time under 10s locally (or marked as slow)
- [ ] ticket or PR referencing sample app and owner

Open questions / TODOs:
- How strict should latency gates be for CI smoke? (tradeoff: flaky vs useful). Propose: measure but don't fail on latency until we have 2 weeks of baseline data.
- Should we expand telemetry assertions to include token_count? pros/cons: useful for regression detection, but brittle across models. Leave as opt-in.
- Add python-headless harness? Right now Playwright covers a browser JS path; need lightweight python CLI smoke runner in pytest that mirrors the same checks.

Example quick debug commands (for devs):
- run single test: npx playwright test tests/onboard.spec.ts --project=chromium -g \"first-run onboarding\"
- collect trace on failure: npx playwright test --trace on --reporter=list
- record HAR: set PLAYWRIGHT_HAR=on in env before running dev server

Notes on sample fixtures & model pinning:
- fixtures/live/ contains recorded minimal responses from the hosted API pinned to model `redwood/gpt-medium-v1` to avoid dim mismatches.
- When updating fixtures, include a small note in PR summarizing changes and add the `fixtures/updated-by` tag.

Appendix: quick PR template (for adding smoke tests)
- Title: tests(smoke): add <short case> for <sample-app>
- Body: short motivation, runtime estimate, owner, linked sampleapp PR
- Checklist: run locally, add trace artifacts on failure, add telemetry stub if network call added

Sign-off: Asha P. (draft). Leaving this as a working doc — intended to be iterated with QA and SRE before moving to final.

Rough contact list:
- devexp: #devexp on Slack
- smoke alerts: #devexp-smoke (auto-posts from CI)

Last notes (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep the smoke suite as minimal as possible: developer-facing regressions only. Anything that is flaky or expensive should be promoted to an integration tier.
- Consider making a tiny 'smoke harness' npm package that samples can `npm run smoke` against to reduce duplication across sampleapps.
